rationale: The source asks to refactor an existing single tool (QSourceTool, wired to querysource's QS()) into a tenant-scoped QuerysourceToolkit that also covers MultiQuery pipelines. Research must (a) pin down the current tool and its consumers, (b) extract the real QS()/MultiQuery contracts from the installed querysource 4.5.11 package (the ../querysource checkout is absent), (c) find how tenancy (program_slug) is modelled, and (d) locate the AbstractToolkit conventions the refactor must follow.

queries.intent: Orient: locate the current QuerySource tool, its sibling sources and any prior SDD tasks touching them.
Read the current QSourceTool: schema, description, how it builds the QS() payload and what it returns.
Read parrot_tools/querytoolkit.py — it may already be a toolkit over querysource and shape the refactor.
Read QuerySlugSource / MultiQuerySlugSource — the other in-repo QS() consumer, to reuse or align payload building.
Extract the QS() constructor/execution contract (slug, conditions, fields, ordering, limit, etc.) from the installed querysource.
Locate the JSON filtering dialect: how conditions/where_cond/filter/fields/ordering/grouping/querylimit are parsed from the request payload.
Read the MultiQuery entrypoint (MultiQS) to learn the pipeline JSON contract and execution API.
Read the MultiQuery component registry — this is what /api/v3/qs/components serializes; the toolkit can call it in-process.
Read the components REST handler to confirm the catalog payload shape shown in the source.
Read the MultiQuery REST handler: how a pipeline is submitted and whether multi-queries can be persisted (the 'API de MultiQuery' the LLM should use to create them).
Find the public.queries model (QueryModel) and the program_slug tenant attribute plus any slug lookup helpers.
Read the queries manager handler: list/get/create slug CRUD the toolkit could delegate to for 'list slugs', 'inspect slug' and 'register multi-query'.
Find existing tenant / program_slug scoping patterns inside ai-parrot (tools, bots, auth) to reuse for toolkit restriction.
Read the AbstractToolkit base to follow its tool-generation, lifecycle (_open/_close, auto_open) and naming conventions.
Find every consumer/export of QSourceTool so the refactor can update callers (hard cut, no shims).
Recent history on the tool and its sibling sources (regression / in-flight work).
Inventory the MultiQuery component families (sources, operators, transformations, destinations) for the catalog the LLM will browse.
Existing test coverage for qsource / querytoolkit / query_slug.
Read a comparable multi-tool toolkit in parrot_tools to mirror structure (tools exposed via methods, Pydantic args).
